items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names like opAddToCart, cartPricing and computeStats make intent clear, but business code is full of single-letter and cryptic names (S, st, u, pr, n, r, a, mut, tx) and dense one-liners such as the renderStats and api.importData bodies.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One new file of ~1327 lines (the >500-line cap applies). It is reasonably layered (op* functions wrapped by mut/tx, shared by UI and API), but long one-liner render functions mix HTML strings and logic, and the close-modal code is repeated in importData, reset and the UI import handler.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: BizError with a tx rollback, validQty, phone checks and normalizeData before import are solid. There are some magic numbers (9999 qty cap, the 500-row log limit), and the parts of the source I can see don't show whether tx catches non-BizError exceptions specifically.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: There is a rules box covering threshold and stacking, plus a sumBox amount breakdown and status badges. Confirm dialogs cover pay/ship/cancel/after-sale, import overwrite and reset (confirmBox ... 'danger'). Import errors are explained in plain language and end with “当前数据未改变” (current data unchanged).

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The API wraps the same op* functions through mut(), which runs them inside tx and then renderAll. Money is in integer cents (toC/toY, amountC, salesC). computeStats is derived from the records on every call, and import runs normalizeData before replacing state. All 25 hidden tests pass.
